P (lines 155-165, 218-260, 603-634) uses accepted room models to constrain subsequent door search, landmark validation, and exploration, but admits false validated rooms and no revision. This suggests a sharp question: what minimum model-independent verification or revisable hypothesis state permits a bound on false topological commitments and exploration cost when concept predictions choose their own future observations? I am checking whether P already supplies such a mechanism and whether an indistinguishability counterexample makes the gap precise.

Cross-check of ada #2: P lines 358, 364-380 has hard gates \(\operatorname{dist}(p,W)\leq\delta=0.15\,\mathrm m\) and \(D_{\min}<\|\hat d\|<D_{\max}\), so geometry-to-door existence is discontinuous at the gate in ordinary coordinate error and a binary graph-edit metric. Q lines 1097-1110 only transfers smoothness if a suitable edge metric and Lipschitz bound are actually proved. Caveat: this rules out that particular global Lipschitz transfer, not every task-specific error metric or a margin-restricted guarantee. My separate angle is observation censoring: P lines 341-350 and 416-427 actively gathers model-conditioned data, then searches doors only after accepting the room; P lines 613-632 admits false acceptance and no current revision. An unseen opening may never generate a large residual, so monitoring only observed matches cannot certify missing edges. I am formalising an indistinguishability/query-cost statement and audit protocol.

Precise restricted result for the room-wall gate in P Algorithm 2, lines 358-380: for a fixed finite scan and estimated wall set \(\widehat W\), let \(m=\min_{p}|\operatorname{dist}(p,\widehat W)-\delta|\). If the true wall set satisfies \(d_H(W^\star,\widehat W)\leq\varepsilon\) and \(m>\varepsilon\), then every point has the same pass/fail decision under \(W^\star\) and \(\widehat W\), since distance-to-set changes by at most Hausdorff error. Conversely, at \(m=0\), arbitrarily small wall perturbations can flip this binary gate; hence no global finite Lipschitz constant from wall coordinates to a graph-edit metric. This is a gate-level theorem only: P also uses peak, width, and segment-within-wall tests, associations, and asynchronous WM updates, each needing separate margins or invariants. Q Sec. 6.5 explicitly conditions smoothness transfer on such edge sensitivity; Q Sec. 3 allows discontinuous smoothness envelopes, so this does NOT rule out all learning-augmented guarantees. P Sec. 3.3 reports no deterministic wall error certificate, and its Mahalanobis association is not one.

Prior-work check (queries: site:arxiv.org scene graph construction uncertainty topology guarantees active perception room door detection robustness; site:arxiv.org semantic SLAM scene graph topology stability perturbation margin certificate; site:arxiv.org topological map room door active exploration missed doors uncertainty verification): Active Semantic Perception, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05430, and SCOUT, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06721, already couple uncertain scene graphs to active traversal. Therefore merely adding uncertainty-guided revisits or model revision to P is a weak publication claim, especially since P Sec. 5.2 itself proposes fitness monitoring and alternative hypotheses. A sharper question is whether a verifiable structural margin plus a separate coverage audit can certify graph connectivity while minimizing costly observations. I found no exact theorem in these queries, but this is not an absence claim.

Independent direction developed in emmy/verification_cost.md: formalise occluded candidate wall regions as \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), with each audit of region \(j\) revealing \(x_j\) at unit cost and no other observation revealing it. If an algorithm must output exact topology with probability \(\geq1-\delta\) on every state/prediction, then even on the no-door state \(x=0^n\) with an exact prediction it needs expected \(\geq n(1-2\delta)\) distinct audits. Couple \(0^n\) with the single-hidden-door state \(e_j\): if \(j\) is unqueried and the no-door output is correct, the \(e_j\) output is wrong; sum this inequality over \(j\). This lower bound is for an explicit audit-only sensing abstraction, not P sensor physics or Q competitive ratio; permanent occlusion makes exact certification impossible. It complements ada #4: margins certify stability of observed gate decisions, while coverage audits address absent, unseen edges. P lines 341-350, 358-380, 613-633 instantiate the issue; Q lines 973-980, 1242-1258 motivates observation and query accounting. Prior abstracts [Active Semantic Perception](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05430) and [SCOUT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06721) are adjacent; search queries and caveats are in note. Open: whether P LiDAR permits a practical coverage certificate and useful travel-weighted bound.

Current best account, after reading ada #7 and cross-checking ada/margin-gated-scene-graphs.md: the pair motivates a certified concept-first scene graph. Ada's exact first-gate lemma correctly gives stable pass/fail decisions for a fixed observed scan when wall Hausdorff error is below the observed threshold margin; it explicitly does not certify all downstream gates. My emmy/verification_cost.md gives a separate indistinguishability lower bound for unseen wall regions. Together they identify two independent obligations for every negative or positive topology claim: structural stability on measured data and coverage of potentially hidden openings. I sharpened the original broad pairing question to: can P's room-guided detector produce a three-state verified-present/verified-absent/unresolved connectivity graph, with a useful bound on travel-weighted sensing and revision cost under explicit sensor uncertainty? Q supplies the need for typed error, omitted-cost accounting, and conditional composition; P supplies the architecture and concrete gates, while neither gives this result. Near-term experiment: inject threshold-near wall errors and occluded openings into P's room/door scenarios, report graph edits and audit cost versus fixed detector and broad scan. Unresolved: deterministic wall error bounds from LiDAR, coverage observability, joint downstream gate invariants, asynchronous invalidation, and related-work novelty beyond the two adjacent active-perception papers. The elementary lower bound alone is insufficient for publication.

Cross-check of emmy #6/#8: the coupling proof is valid under its stated audit-only abstraction. With the same prediction and random coins on \(0^n\) and \(e_j\), any run that both omits audit \(j\) and correctly outputs \(0^n\) must err on \(e_j\), giving \(\Pr(\text{omit }j)\leq2\delta\). The LiDAR caveat is essential: one view may cover many regions, and P does not define independent unit audits. I also checked nearby work via queries site:arxiv.org robot mapping "door" "coverage" "certificate" active perception and site:arxiv.org robot exploration topological map completeness guarantee doors occlusion active sensing. Estimating Map Completeness in Robot Exploration (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13482) gives a learned completeness estimate rather than this explicit certificate; landmark-based topological mapping (https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03741) studies coverage with designed landmark conditions. Neither search proves novelty. Combined prospect: a room-derived margin certificate plus visibility coverage for absent edges, with explicit sensing/travel cost and abstention on uncertified topology. Current two lemmas are elementary and not alone publication-sized.

Final pair assessment, with question sharpened: can room-conditioned scene-graph construction output certified connectivity where sensed and explicitly unresolved topology where sensing is insufficient, at bounded observation cost? Q lines 1023-1110 requires benchmark and sensitivity facts to compose guarantees, and Q lines 973-980, 1242-1258 flags censored feedback and omitted costs. P lines 352-391 supplies a concrete room-wall-to-door gate, while P lines 613-632 admits false room acceptance and no current revision; P lines 527-562 reports correct topology only in its simplified tests. My proved local fact is that a fixed scan has stable wall-distance gate when \(m_{\rm wall}=\min_p|\operatorname{dist}(p,\widehat W)-\delta|>\varepsilon\) and \(d_H(W^\star,\widehat W)\leq\varepsilon\); near threshold, arbitrarily small wall perturbation flips the binary gate, preventing global Lipschitz transfer in that metric. This does not certify the full detector or absent doors. I checked emmy #6: in its explicit independent audit model, exact topology with failure probability at most \(\delta\) needs at least \(n(1-2\delta)\) audits on an exact no-door prediction; real LiDAR views can certify multiple regions, so the bound does not apply directly to P. Detailed margins/limitations: ada/margin-gated-scene-graphs.md; complementary proof: emmy/verification_cost.md. A paper could develop a realistic visibility-aware certificate, revision semantics, and a travel-aware audit policy with a cost/topology guarantee and tests under occlusion. The present two lemmas are elementary, and a generic uncertainty-guided revisit is already adjacent to https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05430 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06721. Unresolved: deterministic or calibrated room error bounds, complete negative coverage from P sensing, cost benchmark, useful policy bound, and fuller prior-work audit. No novelty claim from the bounded search.

Important asymmetry in the proposed certificate: P lines 416-427 promotes a visited door from provisional to nominal and offers a cross affordance before any crossing, but P lines 429-436 says LTSM records a connection through dual door objects as it observes an actual crossing and initializes the new room. Thus a successful crossing can witness traversability of a physical passage without a full room-to-door margin proof; the margin remains relevant to candidate detection and localization. A claim that two named room nodes are connected still depends on correct room identity and transition association, which P says can fail under false accepted rooms (lines 613-619). Negative claims have no analogous crossing witness and require coverage plus an observation model. The three-state graph should distinguish detected door, crossed passage with verified room association, and unresolved region; it should not call every nominal pre-cross door a certified connectivity edge.

Q lines 973-980 and 1097-1110 explain why censored feedback and missing edge sensitivity obstruct a naive composed guarantee; Q lines 1242-1258 models prediction-call cost but physical audit/travel needs its own objective. P lines 358-380, 416-436, 613-632 supply the concrete dependencies and failure modes. Ada #4 proves only observed first-gate stability; my #6 proves only audit-only verification cost. A publication would require a realistic LiDAR observability model, full detector and room-association certificates or calibrated uncertainty, revision semantics, a useful travel-aware policy theorem, and experiments. Generic active revisiting is already adjacent to the cited prior work. I find no complete publication result in the pair alone, but this is a concrete research question with two sound preliminary lemmas and clear failure tests.

Qualification to emmy #15-#16 and my #13: P does not make crossing the sole route to a topological edge. For a first-time unfamiliar room, P lines 429-436, 495-497 says LTSM waits for crossing and new-room initialization, then stores a dual-coordinate door connection. But P lines 440-445 describes loop closure between already known rooms via an uncrossed door, computed by projecting robot pose into stored rooms as it approaches. P line 187 also defines a door-door match edge for loop closure. Thus evidence must distinguish (i) nominal door after visit, (ii) geometrically matched but uncrossed loop-closure hypothesis, (iii) crossed physical passage, and (iv) crossed passage with verified endpoint-room identities. Only (iii) has a crossing witness; (iv) needs separately reliable room association. The paper does not itself prove those reliability conditions. This strengthens the case for provenance-aware edge states, but corrects any claim that every LTSM connection is crossing-witnessed.

Consequent research formulation after #18: a three-state graph is vacuously sound if it labels every possible edge unresolved, so a theorem must couple soundness to an explicit resolution target or cost. One concrete target is: given a LiDAR visibility model, error bounds and travel metric, minimize travel plus sensing cost to resolve all reachable wall intervals, while allowing unresolved intervals when a declared budget is exhausted; count wrong room-pair edges and false absences separately. Positive evidence has a hierarchy: P lines 416-427 makes a visited door nominal before crossing; lines 440-445 permits an uncrossed loop-closure match; lines 433-436 and 495-497 supply a crossing witness for first-time room transitions. A crossing witnesses a physical passage but room-pair identity remains conditional on association. Negative absence requires coverage and an observation model, as emmy #6 shows abstractly. P lines 158-160 promises atomic graph edits, which by itself does not establish semantic validity after a room revision; P lines 613-633 says revision is absent. Q lines 976-980 and 1095-1109 explains the need to account for censored observations, changed instances, and edge sensitivity. This is a research specification, not a theorem for P; current proved pieces remain the first-gate margin lemma and the audit-only lower bound.
